local:dotfiles-command-deprecation.title:
v2026.7.16 (#11436) consolidated dotfiles management under
`mise bootstrap dotfiles` and DEPRECATED the top-level `mise dotfiles` (hidden
now, warnings in 2027.2.0, removal in 2028.2.0). This is the marker that stopped
the 7.16 gate, and it is INERT here: 0 uses of `mise dotfiles` in this repo
(control arm — `mise run` greps to 24 hits in mise.toml, so the probe
discriminates). Recorded like the Tera item so the 2027.2.0 and 2028.2.0
releases are not read as routine, and so a future session does not have to
re-derive that the marker was harmless.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for v2026.8.0: still INERT, but the probe needs a caveat that
did not exist before. Every hit for `mise dotfiles` in this repo is now THIS
item's own text plus prior currency reports — documentation OF the deprecation,
not a use of it. A naive grep returns 8 and reads as a regression: **a watch item
that names a token makes itself grep-positive forever**, so exclude
`currency.toml` and `docs/currency/` or the item refutes its own claim. Control
arm: `mise run` -> 27 hits in `mise.toml`. 2026.8.0 touches `dotfiles add` only
through `config --path <dir>`, which this repo does not use.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-05 for v2026.8.2, with the recorded exclusions applied
(`currency.toml` + `docs/currency/`): **0** uses. Control arm: `mise run` -> 33
hits in `mise.toml`. Still INERT; the 8.2 bootstrap work expands
`mise bootstrap` (the replacement surface), touching no deprecation timeline.

local:min-version-floor-vs-reviewed-vers.title:
Two versions are declared and they mean different things. Keep them
straight on every bump: `currency.toml` `expected` = the version whose notes we
have read (moves every time we review); `mise.toml` `min_version.soft` = the
version we are verified against; `min_version.hard` = the oldest we will run at
all (2026.7.14, where #11269/#11288/#11296 landed). soft must stay ABOVE hard or
it is inert — hard errors across exactly the range soft would warn in.

MOVED 2026-08-03 for v2026.8.0: `soft` 2026.7.18 -> 2026.8.0 in the SAME change as
`expected` above, which is exactly what this item exists to enforce. `hard` stays
at 2026.7.14 — nothing between 7.18 and 8.0 introduces a known-bad behaviour that
would justify raising the floor — and soft (8.0) > hard (7.14), so the warning
band stays observable.

MOVED 2026-08-05 for v2026.8.2: `soft` 2026.8.0 -> 2026.8.2 in the same change as
`expected`, same rule. `hard` stays at 2026.7.14 — 8.1/8.2 add features (remote
task cache, `--affected`, the bootstrap resource system) and fixes; nothing
makes an older mise newly dangerous — and soft (8.2) > hard (7.14).

local:path-dedup-lands-on-the-surface-th.title:
v2026.7.18 (#11491): computed environments (`mise env`, `mise x` child
PATHs, `mise doctor`) now collapse exact duplicate PATH entries first-wins,
fixing runaway `_.path` accumulation in nested shells and IDE terminals that
inherit an activated PATH without mise's state vars. **The live shell PATH is
deliberately left untouched.**

READ THIS ONE CAREFULLY BEFORE CONCLUDING IT FIXED ANYTHING HERE. It lands on
the same surface as the founding defect of this whole engine — `MISE_ENV_CACHE=1`
had baked a stale `.../installs/pipx-graphifyy/0.9.23/bin` into PATH *ahead* of
the mise shims, so every bare `graphify` ran 0.9.23 under a 0.9.25 pin
(`sync.py`'s module docstring). It is NOT the same bug and does not retire
`resolve_from_path` / `_is_mise_shim` / `_mise_shim_dirs`: dedup removes EXACT
duplicates, while ours was a DIFFERENT, stale directory ordered ahead of the
shims — nothing to dedup. And the fix explicitly excludes the live shell PATH,
which is exactly where step 1 looks. Reviewed at the 7.16 -> 7.18 bump.

Nothing else in 7.17/7.18 reaches this repo, checked rather than assumed: the
monorepo/Node-workspace task work (#11466/#11435/#11473/#11476/#11471) needs a
`[monorepo]` table and workspace packages, of which this repo has none;
`idiomatic_version_file_disable_files` (#11470) is unset; `mise prune --tools`
(#11501), the Windows program-resolution fixes (#11486/#11489), GitLab
pagination (#11507), Cargo install options (#11480), Aqua locked HTTP installs
(#11499) and the asdf `bin/list-all` env plumbing (#11492) are all on paths this
repo never takes. #11495 (installing a tool no longer touches loaded config
files) DOES reach `mise install` here and is a pure improvement.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for v2026.8.0, and it lands on this surface AGAIN — read as
carefully as the 7.18 entry above. **hook-env now detects and restores drift**: if
a shell command overwrites a mise-managed variable or removes a PATH entry mise
added, hook-env puts it back.

It does NOT retire `resolve_from_path` / `_is_mise_shim` / `_mise_shim_dirs`, for
the same reason 7.18's dedup did not. Ours is a stale, DIFFERENT directory ordered
AHEAD of the shims — nothing was removed and nothing is duplicated, so neither
dedup nor restore-what-was-removed reaches it. Measured the same day at 0.9.31:
`command -v graphify` still resolves to
`~/.local/share/mise/installs/pipx-graphifyy/<ver>/bin/graphify` rather than a
shim, which is why `mise.toml`'s `GRAPHIFY_MAX_GRAPH_BYTES` does not reach a bare
`graphify` call and why `mise exec -- graphify …` is required above the cap.

Nothing else in 2026.8.0 reaches this repo, checked rather than assumed: the
monorepo workspace inference (#11554 Cargo, #11556 uv, Go, Node) needs workspace
metadata — control-armed, `[tool.uv.workspace]` appears **0** times in
`pyproject.toml`; precompiled Ruby, aqua BOM checksums (#11552), brew-cask pours,
the forgejo `fj` key path (#11545) and the asdf `depends` PATH fix are all on
paths this repo never takes.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-05 for v2026.8.2, and this time NOTHING lands on the PATH
surface — 8.1 is task-cache/`--affected`/config-flag work, 8.2 is bootstrap
provisioning; neither touches how a live shell resolves a binary, so
`resolve_from_path` / `_is_mise_shim` / `_mise_shim_dirs` still stand.
Re-measured the founding symptom the same day: `command -v graphify` in an
inherited shell resolves to `installs/pipx-graphifyy/0.9.32/bin/graphify` — a
STALE install dir, now two versions behind the 0.9.34 pin — while `mise exec --
graphify --version` correctly reports 0.9.34. The skew is live, which is
exactly why step 1 keeps looking at the live shell PATH and why
version-sensitive calls go through `mise exec`.

local:remote-version-fetch-failure-repor.title:
Before v2026.7.16 (#11391) a NETWORK FAILURE while listing remote
versions was reported as "no versions found matching date filter" — an outage
wearing an authoritative empty answer's clothes, which is the exact shape
`.claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md` exists to catch. Fixed in 7.16
(reported as a fetch failure, and memoized per process). Kept as a watch item
because any host still BELOW 7.16 will show the misleading form, so the
signature table in `persistence-gate-retry.md` has to keep both.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-03 for v2026.8.0: unchanged, and still correct to keep. This
host is far above the 7.16 floor so the misleading form cannot appear here; the
item survives for hosts that are not.

RE-PROBED 2026-08-05 for v2026.8.2: unchanged — nothing in 8.1/8.2 touches
remote-version listing's failure reporting. Same disposition.
